##### **Executive Summary** 

##### **Highlights of international copper market** 

In Q4 2011,

copper prices bottomed out, but copper prices were still under pressures due to the uncertainties of Eurozone crisis and negative news in copper market. Worries about future economy are not dispelled although recent America’s economic data was good and Chinese PMI returned to over 50. It is estimated that copper prices in Q1 2012 will remain at a relative low level, fluctuating between US$ 6,500-8,500. In 2012 copper prices will keep a low-high trend, at an average price of US$ 8,000. 

##### **Global refined copper output rises in Q4** 

The refined copper output of the world’s major producing countries all increased in Q4 2011. The refined copper production in Zambia and Mexico kept a rising pace and Japan recovered from the quake. Although Chile’s and Peru’s copper productions were effected, the situation still turned better in the second half of 2011. China’s copper production was also on a high level. But most Chinese copper producers reduced the production in the year end; furthermore, there was still a price inversion between refined copper and copper scrap, so those who use copper scrap for copper producing were in halt production, which might reduced some production. Generally speaking, the Q4 global refined copper production still increased both on a quarterly and yearly basis. 

The consumption of refined copper in US was recovering encouraged by the good-performing economic data; but in Europe, the negative affection of the European Debts Crisis has already shown up; the Chinese copper fabricators needed to withdraw the money and were not willing to produce many copper products. Besides, the slowdown of Chinese economy also gave a negative impact on the copper consumption. So the Q4 copper consumption witnessed a yearly growth and a quarterly drop. 

The global refined copper output was 4.91mlnt, up 6.5% y/y and up 1.0% q/q; the Q4 refined copper consumption was 4.795mlnt, up 5.4% y/y and down slightly 0.2% q/q. The global refined copper output and consumption in 2011 was about 19.158mlnt and 19.216mlnt, up 3.4% and 3.9% both on a yearly basis. The copper market has 58kt shortage in 2011.

Based on the rising copper ore output and expending copper smelting capacity in 2012, Antaike predicted the global refined copper production in 2012 will be 19.83mlnt, with an annual growth rate of 3.5%, a little higher than 2011; the global refined copper consumption is expected to reach 19.8mlnt in 2012, and the growth rate will sl

ow down to around 3.0%. The refined copper market will be comparatively balanced with only a little shortage in 2012, which will support the copper price to some extent. 

##### **Global copper concentrate supply in shortage** 

Strikes were still the negative factor to effect the copper concentrates ever since the fourth quarter, especially Freeport McMoRan’s Grasberg mine in Indonesia. The Grasberg mine was running at low capacity and once stopped production after the strike occurred in min-September. The company’s Cerro Verde mine in Peru restarted production on Nov. 30 after two-month strike, but it still wasted more than a half of the production period in Q4; the Collahuasi copper mine in North Chile kicked off production after a short-time protest which would surely reduce the whole year’s copper conc. production. 

Chinese copper smelters’ demand for copper conc. kept a rising pace stimulated by a high refined copper output. The demand in other countries was stable. 

The world’s copper conc. decreased slightly by 1% y/y to 3.06mlnt and the copper conc. consumption inched up to 3.17mlnt in Q4 which causing the global copper conc. supply shortage at about 90kt. 

The world’s copper conc. production almost didn’t increase in 2011 due to the massive strikes, decreasing ore grade, terrible weather and no new capacity commissioned. The copper conc. consumption increased a little pushed by the expending smelting capacity. So the whole year’s supply shortage extended to 180kt.

##### **Highlights of Chinese copper market** 

In Q4, part of smelters intentionally cut production due to the guaranteed annual production together with low level of TC/RCs. All of above factors resulted in production drawdown of refined copper and blister copper in Q4 (production in Dec is estimated, the same below). Copper blister production was 733kt in Q4, down by 6.9% against Q3. Refined copper production reached 1.27Mt in Q4, down by 7.2% against Q3. Copper concentrate production is relative stable in Q4, only down by 2.5% against Q3 to 320kt. 

Domestic copper production kept a rapid growth in 2011. Of them, copper refined production increased by 12.2% to 5.14Mt; copper blister production reached 2.93Mt, up by 12.1%; copper concentrate production was 1.23Mt, up by 7.9%. 

Import of refined copper increased dramatically to 939kt in Q4 (Dec. data is Antaike’s estimation), only lower than Q2 2009 but one third larger t

han Q3 2011; import of copper conc. also increased by 8.2% to 1.829Mt compared with Q3; import of copper scrap and copper blister maintained the same level as that in Q3; import of copper semis decreased slightly. Affected by weak demand at broad, export of main copper semis continued to decline, down by 13.5% against Q3 to 109kt, export of refined copper was almost stagnant in the same period. ##### **Chinese Copper Price** ##### **Copper price is declining** The copper price bottomed at US$6,635/t on Oct. 3, the lowest level in 2011, and it fluctuated between US$7,000-8,000/t within the year. The European Debts Crisis and the slowdown of China’s economy growth are the two key factors which can affect the metal market in 2011. The average copper price of cash month and 3-month dropped to US$7,488/t and US$7,510/t in Q4 2011, decreasing by 16.72% and 16.66% on a quarterly basis and declining by 13.29% and 12.85% on a yearly basis. But as the prices were higher in the first half compared with the corresponding period of the previous year, the annual average price was still above the level in 2010. Open interest on LME began to increase since late Oct., a high-low trend in Dec. Open interest on COMEX fluctuated down, although total open interest increased gradually since late Nov. Open interest on SHFE fell back after a sharp rise. **Chart 1 Open Interest on World’s Top Three Nonferrous Metals Exchanges (0’000 lots)** 7 ##### **Copper inventory changes on LME and SHFE** In Q4, copper inventory on LME declined to about 370kt at the end of 2011, with a drop of about 100kt. Canc

elled warrants was in a high level, with the highest of over 60kt, at 44kt at the end of 2011, accounting for about 12% of inventory, a sign of continuous decline of inventory. Most of cancelled warrants came from warehouses in Korea and Singapore, indicating that these copper were shipped to China, caused by restocking need in China. 

Indonesia Grasberg mine workers ended strike after Freeport bosses agreed to an increase in wages. Strikes happened in foreign mines increased worries about copper concentrate supply, which formed support for copper prices. 

Inventory on SHFE fell below 100kt after Oct, even below 60kt at the end of Nov. After that, inventory has a rise due to importing large number of refined copper. Inventory on SHFE maintained below 100kt.

##### **Sulfuric acid prices maintains stable** 

In Q4, Chinese sulfuric acid prices had a clear downward trend, at a quarterly average price of 473yuan/t, down by 17.7% y/y and 13.7% against Q3. Sulfuric acid prices decreased clearly in China’s North areas, but stable or a slightly rise in China’s South areas. On the whole, sulfuric acid prices were under pressures in Q4 when domestic export for sulfuric acid was restricted, together with weak demand for sulfuric acid. In addition, declining cost pulled sulfuric acid prices. Global sulphur prices decreased in Q4, which gave pressures on sulfuric acid prices. According to 2012 Chinese import tariffs, import tariff on sulphur was adjusted to 1% from previous 3%, which decreased cost of sulpur import. According to above 

8 

analysis, domestic sulfuric acid is expected to be stable, at the average of 450yuan/t in Q1 2012, with the coming of spring fertilization in China.

##### **Chinese Copper Material Supply** 

##### **Mining capacity** 

In 2011, Chinese newly-added copper concentrate production capacity was about 50-70kt/y, mainly including huangshan (Xinjiang Hami) Nickel-Copper Mine, Tuwu (Xinjiang Hami) Mine, Duobaoshan (Heilongjiang) Copper Mine. These projects will be put into production in H2 2011, and make actual production until 2012. Chinese mining expansion projects since 2011 are as follows: 

**Xinxin Mining Co., Ltd** ’s Huangshan Cu-Ni Mine’s 4,000t/d project started in June, 2010. The mine locates in Hami City, Xinjiang with 84Mt of Cu-Ni ore reserves, including 380kt of nickel content, 220kt of copper content and 32kt of cobalt content. The project with total investment of 1bln yuan will be commissioned by the end of September, 2011. 

**Jiangxi Copper** ’s Dexing Copper Mine will finish 7,500t/d expansion project this year. The total project with 130kt/d capacity is expected to be finished completely in 2012 on schedule. Overall investment budget will reach 2.7bln yuan. After the whole project being commissioned, its mining capacity will rise to 130kt/d from current 100kt/d.

Outputs newly added will include 41kt copper-in-concentrate, 61kg gold and 25t silver. **Chengmenshan Copper Mine** ’s stage 2 of expansion project was kicked off in December, 2009. The stage 2 with investment of 500mln yuan will be constructed for 2 years, and it can process 7000t/d of ores and produce 14.8kt/y of copper in 2012. **Jiangxi Yinshan Mining Co., Ltd** ’s 5,000t/d 

9 

mining project with total investment of 500mln yuan started in January, 2010. After completion, it is expected to produce 6821t metal copper. **Jiangxi Copper** planned to produce 200kt copper –in-concentrate in 2011, up 28kt against that in 2010 

**Zinjin Mining Holdings Group Co., Ltd** ’s Zinjinshan Copper Mine with total investment of 582mln yuan will establish two ore dressing plants which can process 10kt/d and 8,000t/d of ores respectively. And it will also establish a 45kt/d grinding system project. 75% of workshops and foundation engineering will be commissioned in 2011. 

Heilongjiang **Duobaoshan Copper-Molybdenum Mine** is invested by Heilongjiang Duobaoshan Copper Co., Ltd. (Duobaoshan Copper) with a total investment of 3.0bln yuan and planned to be finished by two stages. The first stage is going to be commissioned by the end of 2011. After that it will be capable of processing 25kt ores per day, and producing 117,648t copper concentrates (25% Cu) and 1,401t molybdenum concentrates (45% Mo) per year.  When the second stage being commissioned, 50kt ores can be processed per day, and outputs of copper concentrates (25% Cu) and molybdenum concentrates (45%) will reach 233,316t and 3,014 t respectively. 

**Tuwu Mine** , in Hami, Xinjiang Autonomous Region, was started on Feb. 25, 2010. The project is planned to be finished by two stages. The first stage is open pit project and is going to be commissioned in 2011. After that it will be capable of processing 5kt ores per day in stage 1, and the processing capacity will be expanded to 10kt in stage 2. The project is invested by Xinjiang Huajin Copper Co., Ltd. under Central Asia Huajin Copper Co., Ltd. 

**Xinjiang Hudehe Copper mine** 's 6Mtpy copper mining project kicked off on Sep. 16, which is is a large-scale porphyry copper deposit in Toli County, Tacheng Prefecture, Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region, with proven reserve was 362.5kt metal copper, and 1Mt prospective reserve. The preliminary scheme is to complete 6Mtpy mining project, with total investment budget of 1.47 billion yuan. After being put into production, the project is estimated to produce 15kt copper-in-concentrate. 

**Tongling Tongshan Mining Company** ’s deep mining project started in early September. The project’s designed ores processing capacity is 2kt/d and 660kt/y. The project is designed to produce 5kt copper per year. It is estimated to be completed by the end of 2013.
